leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members prefer Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks as a single two-person part, with near-identical citations built on the magic-wavelength lattice and 1e-18 performance. Eriksson states that he moved to this position from his opening first choice (B020). What is shared: the lattice idea is a distinct invention, the result is measured and reproduced in several laboratories, and the two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist. What is not shared: Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson differ on how far earlier prizes (cooling 1997, comb 2005, ion control 2012) overlap with the lattice step, and on whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to wait. Several supporters flag unverified priority recollection and unclaimed contributors (Lemonde, Ludlow, Bloom, Hinkley, ion-clock groups). Lindroth and Olsson want the citation kept narrow to lattice clocks.

The chair alone prefers Halzen and Karle for the conception and construction of IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth list B007 as an alternative and accept that the diffuse-flux detection is robust, but each places it below B018 mainly because of attribution in a collaboration of hundreds, AMANDA and Baikal precursors, and the omission of Yoshida from a two-name credit. Mehlig regards the three-name version as diluting the instrumentation story. The unidentified origin of most of the diffuse flux is a secondary maturity point. The chair's field is adjacent, which colleagues and the chair himself note.

Johansson alone prefers Cirac and Zoller for the theoretical proposals behind trapped-ion gates and cold-atom quantum simulation. Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth keep B032 as an alternative and agree on originality, maturity and clean two-name credit. The dispute is whether a theory-only prize is coherent given that experiments by Blatt, Wineland, Monroe and others are only partly recognised (2012 recognised control of single quantum systems), and whether B032 overlaps with B015, where Cirac and Zoller also appear with Bloch and Greiner.

Mehlig alone prefers Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert for fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics, and states that no colleague ranked it in the opening. Colleagues who respond (Danielsson, Kroll, Johansson) accept the conceptual quality and experimental confirmation in tweezers, colloids and single molecules, but object to crowded credit, with Crooks the awkward omission, and to its character as a family of exact relations rather than a single measured discovery.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files contain a single-part, single-ballot preferred configuration: five for B018, and one each for B007, B032 and B002.
No member disputes the originality, maturity or independent reproduction of optical lattice clocks, and no member argues that B018 is premature.

B018 has the cleanest attribution claimed on the shortlist: the supporters name Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and first demonstration and Ye for record accuracy and many-body-limited operation, and critics of B018 (Pearce, Johansson, Mehlig as alternative holder) describe the credit as clean.

B007 and B032 recur as alternatives across several files, and members who rank them lower do not dispute the underlying science: the diffuse neutrino flux and the Cirac-Zoller proposals are treated as established.
Several members state that their own field proximity is a bias to be discounted rather than a recusal ground, and that opening-round counts are not scientific merit.
scientific_disputes: Discovery character: whether a precision-metrology advance (B018) is a discovery in physics comparable to opening a new messenger (B007), as Pearce, Danielsson and Lindroth put it, or whether it is a new capability whose measured consequences (relativistic geodesy, constant variation, dark-matter searches) make it one, as the supporters argue.

Whether the lattice-clock step is separable from laser cooling, the frequency comb and ion clocks, or reads as a refinement of already honoured work. Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson raise this against their own first choice and disagree on how heavily it weighs.

Whether a prize for exact fluctuation relations (B002) rewards a phenomenon in nature or mathematical identities confirmed across diffuse platforms, as Danielsson and Kroll question and Mehlig disputes.

Whether the diffuse-flux detection or source identification (TXS 0506+056, Galactic plane) should be the cited basis for B007; the chair prefers the diffuse flux, with source identification as a consequence.
attribution_disputes: B007: two names (Halzen, Karle) against three (adding Yoshida), against a collaboration of hundreds and AMANDA and Baikal predecessors; Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig each raise a version of this, and the chair acknowledges it.

B018: the two-name credit leaves out Lemonde, Ludlow, Bloom, Hinkley and ion-clock pioneers according to Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson; Lindroth and Olsson argue a narrow citation avoids diluting attribution, while Kroll and Eriksson ask whether the clean credit is bought by omission. No member has verified the priority sequence between early lattice proposals and the first operating clocks.

B032 versus B015: Cirac and Zoller appear in both, so a prize on one affects the other; Johansson, Eriksson and Mehlig note the overlap, and Lindroth asks whether Bloch and Greiner would need pairing, which conflicts with the three-person limit.
B002: four credited names for three places; Crooks is the omission Mehlig himself calls awkward, and Danielsson and Kroll cite contested priority for the steady-state fluctuation relation.

B034, B044, B020, B003 (alternatives or secondary mentions only): Eriksson and Mehlig note omissions in a Kane, Mele, Molenkamp configuration (Hasan, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang); Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig note that B044 lacks experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero (for example Cao); Eriksson asks whether Metzner fits a DMFT part; Eriksson and Olsson note Yuasa, Djayaprawira, Butler and Mathon for B003.
maturity_disputes: Whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to wait on B018 (raised as a question by Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson, with Danielsson and Olsson arguing it should not affect timing).
Whether most of the diffuse IceCube flux having no identified source makes B007 premature for a committee wanting a finished story; the chair and Lindroth treat the flux detection itself as secure.

Whether the proximity of the 2025 prize (macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits) and the 2022 prize (Bell tests) bears on B008 and B032; Eriksson, Danielsson, Kroll and Johansson see B008 as adjacent, while Johansson separates B032 from both.
Whether B044 should wait until the pairing mechanism and correlated insulators are better understood and the experimental credit is settled (Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, circuits and circuit QED, Chalmers colleagues linked to the 2025 prize) would recuse himself from any discussion of B008.

Kroll takes part in WACQT management and has quantum-information experience at Lund, and would stay out of any deciding discussion on B008; he also records a research stay in John Hall's laboratory (Hall is not a credited name for B018).

Olsson records academic exchange with Japanese universities including a University of Tokyo fellowship, with Katori based in Japan; she regards it as institutional proximity, not a collaboration, and not requiring recusal. She is also a Chalmers colleague of Johansson, with no apparent link to B018.

Eriksson discloses that his research field (electronic-structure theory, DFT and DFT+DMFT, magnetism) is close to B020, B003, B034 and B044, which he treats as a methodological bias, not a recusal issue.

Mehlig flags intellectual proximity of his stochastic-processes research to B002 as possible bias. Lindroth notes she shares the atomic-physics community with B018, B032 and B015, with no collaboration with a credited name.

Pearce (chair) records PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite and XL-Calibur connections and an astroparticle background adjacent to B007, with no documented tie to Halzen, Karle or Yoshida; flagged as possible bias, not a recusal ground.
questions_for_round2: For B007 versus B018: should a new observational window (IceCube) outrank a measured precision advance (lattice clocks) as a matter of discovery character, or are the five B018 first places evidence that the committee already weighs this the other way?

Can any two- or three-name IceCube credit (Halzen and Karle; or adding Yoshida) be defended against the collaboration, AMANDA and Baikal precursors, and the early concept proponents? If not, would members still prefer B007?

For B018: does the lattice-clock step stand apart from laser cooling (1997), the optical comb (2005) and ion control (2012), and what citation wording (magic-wavelength lattice versus optical clocks generally) keeps the credit specific without excluding Lemonde, Ludlow, Bloom and ion-clock groups?

Should the pending redefinition of the second delay or influence the timing of a B018 prize, and does any member verify the priority between the early lattice proposals and the first operating clocks?

For B032: is a theory-only prize for Cirac and Zoller coherent given the 2012 prize, and should B032 and B015 be treated as one achievement or two, with what consequence for Bloch and Greiner under a three-person limit?

For B002: can members name which result (steady-state fluctuation relation, Jarzynski equality, trajectory-level entropy production) is the cited discovery, and who among Evans, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert is the least dispensable?
Would any member whose first choice is not B018 (Pearce, Johansson, Mehlig) move to it, or would any B018 supporter move to B007, B032 or B002, and on what specific ground?
summary.chair_observation: On explicit first-round positions, five members prefer B018 and three prefer different candidates (B007, B032, B002) in single-part configurations; the disagreement concerns weighing discovery character against attribution clarity more than disputing the science of any leading candidate. B007 and B032 are the most frequent alternatives and share an attribution or credit-scope problem rather than a maturity problem. The chair holds B007 as his own first choice and records that this is an adjacent field.
